title: USGS River Gauge Levels
description: Monitors real-time water gauge levels from USGS Water Services for critical commodity transport waterways. Tracks the Mississippi River at Memphis (gauge 07032000), Ohio River at Cairo (03612500), Columbia River at The Dalles (14105700), and the Missouri River at Omaha (06610000). These gauges are leading indicators for barge traffic disruptions - when the Mississippi drops below 9 feet at Memphis, 60% of US grain exports bottleneck and commodity futures spike. The 2022 low-water event tripled barge rates. Computes rate-of-change to predict threshold breaches days in advance. Pairs with weather data to build a commodity disruption early warning system. No API key required.
code:
import pandas as pd
import requests
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone

now_epoch = int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp())

# USGS Water Services - Instantaneous Values
# Parameter 00065 = Gauge height (feet)
# Docs: https://waterservices.usgs.gov/docs/instantaneous-values/
GAUGES = {
    '07032000': {'name': 'Mississippi River at Memphis TN', 'critical_low_ft': 9.0, 'commodity': 'grain'},
    '03612500': {'name': 'Ohio River at Cairo IL', 'critical_low_ft': 15.0, 'commodity': 'coal'},
    '14105700': {'name': 'Columbia River at The Dalles OR', 'critical_low_ft': 5.0, 'commodity': 'wheat'},
    '06610000': {'name': 'Missouri River at Omaha NE', 'critical_low_ft': 8.0, 'commodity': 'agriculture'},
}

site_ids = ','.join(GAUGES.keys())
url = (
    'https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/iv/'
    '?format=json'
    '&sites=' + site_ids +
    '&parameterCd=00065'
    '&siteStatus=active'
)
resp = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()

rows = []
time_series = data.get('value', {}).get('timeSeries', [])
for ts in time_series:
    site_code = ts.get('sourceInfo', {}).get('siteCode', [{}])[0].get('value', '')
    site_name = ts.get('sourceInfo', {}).get('siteName', '')
    gauge_info = GAUGES.get(site_code, {})

    values = ts.get('values', [{}])[0].get('value', [])
    if not values:
        continue

    # Take the most recent reading
    latest = values[-1]
    gauge_ft = float(latest.get('value', 0))
    reading_time = latest.get('dateTime', '')

    critical = gauge_info.get('critical_low_ft', 10.0)
    margin_ft = round(gauge_ft - critical, 2)

    if margin_ft <= 0:
        status = 'CRITICAL'
    elif margin_ft <= 2:
        status = 'WARNING'
    elif margin_ft <= 5:
        status = 'WATCH'
    else:
        status = 'NORMAL'

    # Compute rate of change if multiple readings exist
    rate_ft_per_hr = 0.0
    if len(values) >= 2:
        prev = values[0]
        prev_ft = float(prev.get('value', 0))
        rate_ft_per_hr = round((gauge_ft - prev_ft) / max(len(values) - 1, 1), 4)

    rows.append({
        'site_id': site_code,
        'site_name': gauge_info.get('name', site_name),
        'gauge_height_ft': round(gauge_ft, 2),
        'critical_threshold_ft': critical,
        'margin_ft': margin_ft,
        'rate_ft_per_reading': rate_ft_per_hr,
        'status': status,
        'primary_commodity': gauge_info.get('commodity', ''),
        'reading_time': reading_time,
        '_epoch': now_epoch,
    })

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
if not df.empty:
    df = df.sort_values('margin_ft').reset_index(drop=True)
GENERATE_RESULTS(df)
